question:
(i) Explain the photon picture of radiation using the relation $E=h\nu$.
(ii) A hydrogen atom emits radiation when its electron jumps from an energy level $-1.51\,\text{eV}$ to $-3.40\,\text{eV}$. Calculate the energy of the emitted photon in eV and explain why this corresponds to a spectral line.

options.A:
(i) Photon energy is $E=\dfrac{h}{\nu}$.
(ii) $E_{\text{photon}}=-1.89\,\text{eV}$, so no spectral line occurs.
options.B:
(i) Radiation interacts as photons with energy $E=h\nu$.
(ii) $E_{\text{photon}}=E_i-E_f=(-1.51)-(-3.40)=1.89\,\text{eV}$. This definite energy difference gives a definite frequency, hence a spectral line.
options.C:
(i) A photon has rest mass and energy $E=mv^2$.
(ii) $E_{\text{photon}}=4.91\,\text{eV}$ and it produces a continuous spectrum.
options.D:
(i) Radiation exchanges energy continuously.
(ii) $E_{\text{photon}}=0.56\,\text{eV}$ because hydrogen levels are continuous.
